newsitem.title: KENYA: Zaire rebels seek neutral site for delayed talks.
newsitem.headline: Zaire rebels seek neutral site for delayed talks.

text.p: Zaire rebels said there would be no talks with President Mobutu Sese Seko on Thursday if the location was Congo's Pointe Noire port and insisted talks be held in international waters.

"We are not going to have the talks in Pointe Noire and apparently Mr Mobutu doesn't want to go to the international waters so the talks will not talk place today (Wednesday) or tomorrow," rebel Justice "Commissioner-General" Mwenze Kongolo told Reuters by telephone.

"We are talking to the South Africans and there is no problem. The only thing we are requiring to do is go to a neutral place and we are still prepared to go," Kongolo said speaking from the Angolan enclave of Cabinda.
He said the rebel advance on Kinshasa was continuing despite the prospective talks, but gave no details.
On the subject matter of talks Kongolo said: "We came here to hear his (Mobutu's) answer to our proposals and they include his departure."
Rebels earlier argued Pointe Noire port was "enemy ground" and said Mobutu was healthy enough to travel on the South African icebreaker Outeniqua to international waters.
South African Deputy Foreign Minister Aziz Pahad said talks scheduled for Wednesday were postponed, probably until Thursday.
South African President Nelson Mandela, trying to broker a deal to avert a battle for Zaire's capital Kinshasa, waited for Kabila in Pointe Noire on Wednesday where the ship was moored.
Mobutu also waited at Pointe Noire from Kinshasa for the talks.
Zaire rebels have seized three quarters of the country since October in a campaign to oust Mobutu, Zaire's president since 1965 but now ailing with cancer.
